observed_negative_evidence.finding: Two different research_id/claim path names represented the same AgentExit repo pin and E1 source-read objective. Exact-path create-only semantics did not collide; reconciliation later collapsed them to one result.
A new pyvene E1 claim was created under a new research ID even though an older pyvene E2 result already existed; duplicate work stopped only after commit-history discovery.
File-based claim creation on one fast-moving main branch can conflict even for non-overlapping claim paths; Git refs were mapped as a lower-contention create-only coordination primitive.

gap_in_existing_ref_hypothesis.problem: research_id and free-form claim_target are aliases chosen by workers, so semantically identical work can intentionally or accidentally hash differently; including a whole moving main SHA would also create false distinctions after unrelated commits
gap_in_existing_ref_hypothesis.required_change: derive coordination identity from normalized research semantics, not worker-selected naming or unrelated repository motion

stage_dominance_rule.reason: Exact stage equality is insufficient: the pyvene negative result shows that a pre-existing E2 can subsume a later attempted E1 under another ID.
rule: Before claiming, resolve all active/terminal objective records for semantic_subject_key.
A terminal result at a strictly higher evidence stage subsumes a lower requested prerequisite stage when source pin, target scope and relevant architecture digest match.
An active prerequisite stage blocks dependent higher-stage work until its terminal result is consumed unless the protocol explicitly admits parallelism.
E3 upstream-claim identities and E4 fixture digests remain distinct; stage rank alone must not collapse different claims or experiments.
A relevant architecture digest change creates REVIEW with parent_objective_key; unrelated main commits do not create a new semantic objective.
REPLICATION is never inferred from a new research_id; it requires explicit parent_objective_key plus declared replication purpose.

predicted_replay_on_observed_failures.AgentExit: both alias claims map to one subject/objective key and the second create-only ref acquisition loses before source archaeology
predicted_replay_on_observed_failures.pyvene: the later E1 resolves the same subject key and sees an already-terminal E2 that subsumes E1, so no duplicate source read starts
predicted_replay_on_observed_failures.hot_main: ownership acquisition touches an objective-specific Git ref instead of committing the mutex to the shared main head; claim/result materialization can reconcile later

serious_counterhypotheses: Semantic normalization can over-collapse genuinely different research questions if target scope or stage discriminators are too coarse.
Maintaining both ref coordination and pending_research.sqlite discovery may cost more complexity than the duplicate work it saves at low concurrency.

Repository renames, forks and moving default branches can destabilize string-based source identity; stable repository IDs should be preferred where obtainable, while exact commit/tree pins remain mandatory for source evidence.
Relevant-architecture digests can miss an indirect dependency unless the dependency closure is explicit; fail closed to STALE_REVIEW_REQUIRED when impact cannot be bounded.
